reason: I re-ran all three scratchpad scripts and the numbers match exactly. Same-frame nearest-neighbour counts below 1/2/3 um: exp85a 6/34/100, exp87a 24/134/210, exp56 2/18/58. exp87a has 67 pairs below 2 um; before CI, 52 of them were at least 2 um apart and 41 at least 3 um, and every one of them is in a track. The hybrids (104 nodes reverted at the 2 um cutoff, 134 at 3 um) score the same as exp87a on all 4 clips (05b6 TP 834 FP 11; 05db TP 1116 FP 93). So the B31 premise really is false on the final x138/CI outputs. exp85a even has one pair at 0.00 um before CI. I did find one hole in the reasoning. eval_clip matches nodes to GT within 7.0 um (tools/overlap_lab.py l.252-277), so an identical hybrid score alone does not prove the pairs are on unannotated cells. I checked this directly with scratchpad r44v/gt_near.py. Only 2 of the 104 reverted nodes are within 7 um of any same-frame GT node, both on 6bba_05db0fb1, which is about the 1.6 you would expect by chance. That supports the claim for 102 of 104 nodes, and the other 2 do not change the score. The size bound holds: the converged nodes are 0.09-0.11% of 122,328 nodes, so realistically ~0.0003 and at most ~0.002 even under dense annotation. The CI sign is already hedged by #37. The finding proposes no build, no dummy, no slot use and no change to the pair, so rules R1-R10, the schedule, runtime and the byte-identical requirement are not touched. Slot 2 is closed anyway (R40-A1). The proposed post-deadline gate is sensible: RESULTS.md l.130 shows GT itself has 0/0/2 nodes below 1/2/3 um, so pairs below 2 um are not biology.
